title: The response data behind receptor selection
caption: All 2,640 curated Hallem receptor–odorant responses. Columns retain odorant-ID order; the CSV gives the chemical identities. Red and blue indicate positive and negative recorded responses. These are published electrophysiological measurements, not new team experiments. Published data source: ( Hallem & Carlson, 2006 ) .

title: Choosing the first receptors
caption: Published mean responses for the five-receptor screening panel, comparing the selected mold-related odorants with controls. Or35a (one of the named Drosophila melanogaster odorant receptors in our design panel) and Or22a show the largest positive panel differences here. These are literature measurements, not team-generated functional tests; panel preference does not establish specificity to mold. Published data source: ( Hallem & Carlson, 2006 ) .

title: Prediction comparison
caption: Prediction for held-out receptors. R² (coefficient of determination; 1 is perfect, 0 matches the mean baseline, and negative values are worse) rises with sequence information. The full feature set adds only 0.0031 over the ligand (a molecule that can bind to a receptor; here, the tested odorant) + sequence baseline (paired 95% interval −0.0316 to 0.0344). Values come from matched out-of-fold predictions on 2,640 receptor–odorant pairs; this is not a biological intervention result. Published data source: ( Hallem & Carlson, 2006 ) .

title: Which information improves generalization?
caption: Matched feature ablation on unseen chemical clusters and unseen receptors. L: ligand (a molecule that can bind to a receptor; here, the tested odorant) ; S: sequence/ESM2 (protein language model used here to turn sequences into numerical features) ( Lin et al., 2023 ) ; P: pocket (a local cavity in the receptor that can accommodate the ligand) ; D: docking (computationally placing and scoring ligand poses in a receptor) ( Trott & Olson, 2010 ) /contact; M: multiple poses. All groups use the same data, estimator settings and folds. The small full-model gain over LS on unseen receptors has an interval spanning zero; these bars alone do not establish significance. Published data source: ( Hallem & Carlson, 2006 ) .

title: Measured odorant spectra
caption: Six accepted NIST (US National Institute of Standards and Technology; its Chemistry WebBook supplies spectral records) gas-phase spectra after background correction and area normalization. Peak patterns describe relative molecular absorption, not receptor activity or (odorant receptor, the odor-selective subunit) ( Zhao et al., 2024 ) absolute absorption strength. ( NIST, n.d. )

title: Measured IR and size ablation
caption: All variants use the same 82 odors and fixed folds. Removing molecular weight differs from removing all three size-related descriptors. IR (infrared absorption: how a molecule absorbs light at different vibrational frequencies) did not improve chemical-holdout R² (coefficient of determination; 1 is perfect, 0 matches the mean baseline, and negative values are worse) in either model; full paired intervals are downloadable.

title: Equal-mode EVA versus intensity-weighted IR
caption: Descriptors computed from two published harmonic mode sets, with the same Gaussian width and grid. The ordinate scales differ because EVA (a fixed-length descriptor formed by smoothing equally weighted normal-mode frequencies) weights modes equally and computed IR (infrared absorption: how a molecule absorbs light at different vibrational frequencies) uses intensities. Shading marks frequencies below the measured-IR window. This is not a measured spectrum or (odorant receptor, the odor-selective subunit) ( Zhao et al., 2024 ) a receptor-bound calculation. ( Turner & Willett, 2000 ; Harada et al., 2025 )

title: Quantum feature comparison
caption: The 85-odorant comparison includes full EVA (a fixed-length descriptor formed by smoothing equally weighted normal-mode frequencies) ( Turner & Willett, 2000 ) , computed IR (infrared absorption: how a molecule absorbs light at different vibrational frequencies) , training-fold-only PCA (principal component analysis, which compresses features along directions of greatest variation) and random-feature controls. PCA moves chemical-holdout scores closer to baseline but does not exceed it. These are predictions of published functional responses. ( Hallem & Carlson, 2006 )

title: Measured and computed spectra on the same odors
caption: All models are retrained on the same 67-odorant overlap. Different spectral ranges, dimensions and normalization remain part of the comparison; it cannot isolate source accuracy. Scores should not be compared directly to the larger cohorts.

title: Does an odor-perception AI improve receptor predictions?
caption: Matched 109-odorant comparison. All variants retain molecular weight and sequence features. The second fixed checkpoint is a sensitivity analysis, not a selected best model. Chemical-group holdout applies to downstream response labels; upstream molecular exposure is possible. ( Lee et al., 2023 ; Barsainyan et al., 2023 )

title: Predicted versus measured response
caption: Out-of-fold predictions for the chemical-group holdout, baseline versus added POM (Principal Odor Map; OpenPOM is its open-source reproduction for learned molecular odor features) ( Lee et al., 2023 ; Barsainyan et al., 2023 ) . Each point is a receptor–odorant pair; shared receptors and chemicals mean points are not independent experimental replicates. The dashed line denotes perfect prediction. ( Hallem & Carlson, 2006 )

title: Do the improvements survive uncertainty?
caption: Points show added-feature ΔR² (difference in R² between the compared models) ; lines show paired group-bootstrap (resampling observations or groups to assess statistical uncertainty) 95% intervals conditional on fixed predictions. Each row uses its own eligible cohort and matched baseline, not a common ranking of features. A line crossing zero does not establish a reliable gain; secondary intervals are unadjusted.

title: Do the proposed mutations improve panel preference?
caption: Common-box docking (computationally placing and scoring ligand poses in a receptor) comparison against each wild-type receptor. Dots show mean shifts; bars span the minimum and maximum across docking searches, not a confidence interval. The shift is mean ΔVina (mutant docking score minus the corresponding wild-type score) for controls minus mean ΔVina for the mold-related panel; positive values favor the selected mold-related panel. No candidate stays positive across the searches. This scoring diagnostic does not establish an affinity or (odorant receptor, the odor-selective subunit) ( Zhao et al., 2024 ) functional change. Structure / method references: ( Mirdita et al., 2022 ; Trott & Olson, 2010 ) .

title: Checking the proposed mutation mechanism
caption: Minimum mutated-side-chain distance to each odorant in the historical top docking (computationally placing and scoring ligand poses in a receptor) pose. Blue outlines mark distances ≤4.5 Å (ångström; 1 Å = 0.1 nm) . F34Y (residue 34: phenylalanine → tyrosine) and E196Q (residue 196: glutamate → glutamine) are distant from the ligand (a molecule that can bind to a receptor; here, the tested odorant) in these poses; I87V (residue 87: isoleucine → valine) illustrates that geometrical contact alone does not establish improved panel selectivity. Values are pose-level geometry, not binding energies. Structure / method references: ( Mirdita et al., 2022 ; Trott & Olson, 2010 ) .

title: Fly-trained predictions versus mosquito measurements
caption: Each point is one of 2,000 mosquito receptor–odorant pairs across 50 Anopheles receptors and 40 shared odorants. The fly-trained ExtraTrees (an ensemble of decision trees with randomized splitting rules) baseline has R² (coefficient of determination; 1 is perfect, 0 matches the mean baseline, and negative values are worse) = −0.288 and Spearman ρ (rank correlation, from −1 to +1; it measures ordering, not prediction accuracy as a percentage) = −0.060. The dashed line is perfect agreement, not a fitted trend. Observed responses come from Carey et al.; predictions come from this project. Receptors and odorants are shared across points, so the points are not independent biological replicates. Published data source: ( Hallem & Carlson, 2006 ; Carey et al., 2010 ) .

title: Sequence methods for finding functional analogues
caption: All twelve tested sequence methods on the primary 48 × 24 receptor-pair set. Points show agreement between sequence scores and Pearson (correlation measuring linear similarity between numerical profiles) similarity of the 40-odorant response profiles; bars are receptor-bootstrap (resampling observations or groups to assess statistical uncertainty) intervals. The leading 31-aa (amino-acid residues) reciprocal method reaches Spearman ρ (rank correlation, from −1 to +1; it measures ordering, not prediction accuracy as a percentage) = 0.141, but its BH-adjusted (Benjamini–Hochberg multiple-testing correction; q is the adjusted p-value reported here) ( Benjamini & Hochberg, 1995 ) q = 0.259 does not meet 0.05. Methods were selected using the same matrix. This is an exploratory profile-matching analysis, not a validated odor-response predictor. Published data source: ( Hallem & Carlson, 2006 ; Carey et al., 2010 ) .

title: Uncertainty in rebuilt Orco regions
caption: AlphaFold (AI system that predicts protein 3D structures from sequence) confidence summaries for the three missing Orco (odorant-receptor co-receptor, a shared partner that forms the channel with the odor-selective OR) segments in 8V02 (PDB ID for the experimentally determined o-cresol-bound OR10–Orco complex) . Higher pLDDT (predicted local structure confidence on a 0–100 scale; higher is more confident) indicates greater local confidence; larger loop-to-core PAE (predicted aligned error, an estimate of uncertainty in relative residue placement; lower is more confident) indicates less certain relative placement. The long 244–312 loop has particularly uncertain placement. Confidence is inherited from the template prediction and does not validate the subsequently rebuilt, relaxed coordinates. Structure / method references: ( Zhao et al., 2024 ; Jumper et al., 2021 ) .

title: The original bound-state MD diagnostics
caption: Completed bound-state trajectories to 20 ns (nanoseconds, 10⁻⁹ seconds) . Lines show 0.1 ns-bin medians, except hydrogen-bond geometry, shown as the within-bin fraction. Shading marks the prespecified 15–20 ns analysis window. Temperature and membrane readouts coexist with continued rebuilt-region drift. Geometry checks passed, but the trajectories do not establish equilibrium, binding affinity or (odorant receptor, the odor-selective subunit) ( Zhao et al., 2024 ) an experimentally validated loop conformation.

title: Where is the odorant in the receptor complex?
caption: Cα (alpha-carbon atoms, used to trace the protein backbone) traces and o-cresol (2-methylphenol, the odorant resolved in 8V02) heavy atoms from experimental PDB (Protein Data Bank, the archive of molecular 3D structures) ( Berman et al., 2000 ) 8V02 (PDB ID for the experimentally determined o-cresol-bound OR10–Orco complex) . Teal is OR10 (odorant receptor 10 from Aedes aegypti, the yellow-fever mosquito) , gray-green the three Orco (odorant-receptor co-receptor, a shared partner that forms the channel with the odor-selective OR) subunits, and orange the odorant. Missing resolved-chain segments remain disconnected. The tan band is a homology-transferred membrane-orientation reference, not observed lipids. This figure shows the structural starting reference, not an MD (molecular dynamics: computing atomic motion step by step from a force field) ( Eastman et al., 2024 ) trajectory. Experimental structure source: ( Zhao et al., 2024 ) .

title: Which parts move during odorant-free MD?
caption: Recorded 5 ns (nanoseconds, 10⁻⁹ seconds) trajectories of the two rebuilt apo (the odorant-free state) starting models. All three readouts use the same fit to resolved-core Cα (alpha-carbon atoms, used to trace the protein backbone) atoms and measure displacement from each starting structure. Rebuilt regions cover the modeled missing parts of the complex, not only OR10 (odorant receptor 10 from Aedes aegypti, the yellow-fever mosquito) ( Zhao et al., 2024 ) . The shaded first 1 ns includes heating and staged restraint release; the remaining 4 ns are unrestrained. Larger motion in rebuilt regions motivates structural uncertainty checks; these short trajectories do not demonstrate equilibrium or (odorant receptor, the odor-selective subunit) correct loop reconstruction.

title: Odor-response ranking
caption: Retrospective ranking of 29 odorants from one published calcium-response assay (a defined experimental test of biological activity) . Points show Spearman ρ (rank correlation, from −1 to +1; it measures ordering, not prediction accuracy as a percentage) ; intervals are exploratory odor-bootstrap (resampling observations or groups to assess statistical uncertainty) intervals and omit experimental measurement uncertainty. MD (molecular dynamics: computing atomic motion step by step from a force field) ( Eastman et al., 2024 ) ensembles did not outperform static 8V00 (PDB ID for the experimentally determined odorant-free OR10–Orco complex) ( Zhao et al., 2024 ) . The aromatic-ring-count comparison (ρ = 0.790) was an exploratory chemical baseline added after inspecting the panel. Published data source: ( Bohbot et al., 2011 ) .

title: See the odorants behind the correlation
caption: Each panel contains the same 29 odorants. Our docking (computationally placing and scoring ligand poses in a receptor) ( Trott & Olson, 2010 ) scores are compared with AaOR10 (odorant receptor 10 from Aedes aegypti, the yellow-fever mosquito) ( Zhao et al., 2024 ) calcium responses digitized from Bohbot et al. (2011), Figure 2; these are literature measurements, not our wet-lab results. The horizontal axis reverses the Vina (AutoDock Vina docking score; lower scores are more favorable in this model, not a measured response) ( Eberhardt et al., 2021 ) score so stronger predicted docking lies to the right. Color identifies aromatic chemistry. The scatter exposes substantial response variation at similar scores; ensemble docking has not established a calibrated sensitivity or (odorant receptor, the odor-selective subunit) EC50 (concentration producing half the maximal response in a specified functional assay) predictor. Published data source: ( Bohbot et al., 2011 ) .

title: The first functional panel and static docking controls
caption: Top: published AaegOR10 (odorant receptor 10 from Aedes aegypti, the yellow-fever mosquito) ( Zhao et al., 2024 ) /AaegOrco (the odorant-receptor co-receptor from Aedes aegypti) oocyte currents normalized to 3-methylindole, with mean ± SEM (standard error of the mean, describing uncertainty in an estimated mean) from nine oocytes per odorant. A zero SEM for the normalization reference is not evidence of noise-free measurement. Bottom: this project’s static docking (computationally placing and scoring ligand poses in a receptor) ( Trott & Olson, 2010 ) scores versus the same seven response means. The assay (a defined experimental test of biological activity) uses a different Orco (odorant-receptor co-receptor, a shared partner that forms the channel with the odor-selective OR) from the structural complex, and screening concentration remains unresolved. This panel is analyzed separately from the 29-odorant calcium assay. Published data source: ( Pullmann-Lindsley et al., 2024 ) .

title: Three ways to increase receptor encounters
caption: Placement schemes used to distinguish diffusion to the receptor from pocket (a local cavity in the receptor that can accommodate the ligand) entry. Orange shapes indicate initial odorant positions; the first panel shows alternative water and interface placements. The drawings do not show observed trajectories. More available molecules or (odorant receptor, the odor-selective subunit) ( Zhao et al., 2024 ) a shorter starting distance did not establish sustained entry in the analyzed simulations. The concentration comparison remains exploratory.

title: Distance and contacts during attempted entry
caption: Actual unrestrained trajectories from water, membrane-interface and near-entrance placements, shown as 20 ps (picoseconds, 10⁻¹² seconds) -bin medians. A/B identify the two starting models; all analyzed trajectories are included. Dashed lines mark the separate entry components: pocket (a local cavity in the receptor that can accommodate the ligand) distance ≤0.5 nm (nanometers; 1 nm = 10⁻⁹ meters) and contact with at least four pocket residues (within 0.45 nm), jointly sustained for 100 ps. The full-frame analysis found no entry. The 2 ns (nanoseconds, 10⁻⁹ seconds) and 10 ns observation windows differ, so this plot does not estimate comparative entry probabilities.

title: Two different targets for an applied force
caption: Left: SMD (steered molecular dynamics: MD with an applied guiding force) ( Isralewitz et al., 2001 ) couples the odorant to a moving target using a spring. Right: a separate protocol guides S3/S6 (labels for the third and sixth membrane-spanning helices of OR10) ( Zhao et al., 2024 ) reference distances while applying no direct pulling force to the odorant. Blue arrows indicate imposed guidance, not observed trajectories. Both protocols test constrained conditions and do not measure natural entry or (odorant receptor, the odor-selective subunit) exit rates.

title: Entrance motion and odorant release are different readouts
caption: Recorded 70 ns (nanoseconds, 10⁻⁹ seconds) trajectories for two starting conformations. Upper panels show the mismatch of S3/S6 (labels for the third and sixth membrane-spanning helices of OR10) ( Zhao et al., 2024 ) reference distances to apo (the odorant-free state) values; lower panels show odorant distance from the pocket (a local cavity in the receptor that can accommodate the ligand) center. Lines are 0.1 ns-bin medians for readability. Shading marks the final bias-removal interval. The full saved-frame analysis found no sustained exit; a decrease in entrance-distance error is not evidence of a passable tunnel.

title: Look at the structures saved during MD
caption: Coordinates from one entrance-guided A trajectory, saved at 7.6, 27.6, 69 and 70 ns (nanoseconds, 10⁻⁹ seconds) . All frames are aligned on OR10 (odorant receptor 10 from Aedes aegypti, the yellow-fever mosquito) ( Zhao et al., 2024 ) Cα (alpha-carbon atoms, used to trace the protein backbone) atoms to the first displayed frame and shown in one fixed projection at the same scale. Teal and purple highlight pocket (a local cavity in the receptor that can accommodate the ligand) -adjacent segments 117–139 and 281–299; orange shows actual o-cresol (2-methylphenol, the odorant resolved in 8V02) heavy atoms. The last frame follows bias removal. Local geometry changes while the ligand (a molecule that can bind to a receptor; here, the tested odorant) remains near the pocket. A two-dimensional projection cannot establish clearance, and selected snapshots do not show a continuous entry or (odorant receptor, the odor-selective subunit) exit path.

title: Short versus extended entrance guidance
caption: Entrance-distance RMSE (root-mean-square error relative to the selected reference values) over the last 100 ps (picoseconds, 10⁻¹² seconds) before bias removal, compared with time-matched unsteered controls. Each starting conformation is shown separately. The extended protocol changes both target-ramp duration and holding time. Lower RMSE means closer to the selected apo (the odorant-free state) distances, not a wider or (odorant receptor, the odor-selective subunit) ( Zhao et al., 2024 ) passable tunnel. The comparison is descriptive and uses correlated trajectories.

title: Candidate space before full-ligand testing
caption: Candidate spherical-probe radius lower bounds from one guided trajectory, comparing 0.10 and 0.05 nm (nanometers; 1 nm = 10⁻⁹ meters) grids and protein-only versus protein-plus-lipid obstacles. Open triangles show finer-grid evaluations. Each obstacle model selects from the same candidate pool and may choose a different path. These are static centerline diagnostics, not observed ligand (a molecule that can bind to a receptor; here, the tested odorant) routes or (odorant receptor, the odor-selective subunit) ( Zhao et al., 2024 ) independent timepoint experiments; grid sensitivity limits claims of a converged channel width.

title: Inline method schematic
caption: Conceptual illustration, not a molecular trajectory or (odorant receptor, the odor-selective subunit) ( Zhao et al., 2024 ) a validated tunnel. Green shapes represent the receptor environment, tan circles nearby lipids, and the orange shape the odorant. Candidate geometry, steric feasibility and observed passage are separate tests.
note: Diagram is built directly in the HTML.

title: Does the ligand follow the pulling target?
caption: Recorded outward SMD (steered molecular dynamics: MD with an applied guiding force) ( Isralewitz et al., 2001 ) along two candidate corridors at two nominal target speeds. Time begins after the common 0.1 ns (nanoseconds, 10⁻⁹ seconds) baseline; lines are 20 ps (picoseconds, 10⁻¹² seconds) -bin medians. The target is held when lag or (odorant receptor, the odor-selective subunit) ( Zhao et al., 2024 ) force becomes too large, producing plateaus. Target path arc, actual ligand (a molecule that can bind to a receptor; here, the tested odorant) –pocket (a local cavity in the receptor that can accommodate the ligand) distance and bias force are separate readouts: advancing the target did not establish ligand escape. The receptor and surrounding environment were flexible during these runs; applied force is not a measured natural exit barrier.

title: Does a longer local wait relieve the obstruction?
caption: The target was held fixed after lag developed in the slower pulling condition. This plot shows the extension from 0.5 to 2 ns (nanoseconds, 10⁻⁹ seconds) of total fixed-target waiting, at the original 2 ps (picoseconds, 10⁻¹² seconds) sampling. Catch-up requires both axial lag ≤0.20 nm (nanometers; 1 nm = 10⁻⁹ meters) and bias force ≤100 kJ/mol/nm (about 166 pN); orange diamonds mark individual frames meeting both. These brief events did not persist for 100 ps and no sustained exit was observed. Longer local waiting alone has not resolved the blockage in the tested window.

title: Do other receptor conformations open a route?
caption: Peak positive Lennard–Jones (an atomic interaction potential; only its positive repulsive part is summed in our clash scans) repulsion along selected whole-ligand (a molecule that can bind to a receptor; here, the tested odorant) paths, including protein and lipids. Each starting structure contributes snapshots at the indicated times, evaluated separately in two corridors. Lower values mean fewer severe clashes in this diagnostic, not a validated passage. Even the lowest path peak is far above its native-pose reference; these are not free-energy barriers. Related snapshots are not independent experiments.

title: Locate the obstruction along a candidate path
caption: Detailed static placement scan for the 69 ns (nanoseconds, 10⁻⁹ seconds) entrance-guided A snapshot: the lower corridor has the lowest combined repulsion peak among the evaluated selected paths. Top panels score the same ligand (a molecule that can bind to a receptor; here, the tested odorant) poses with protein alone and with protein plus lipids; the dotted line is the native-pose reference (~23 kJ/mol). Bottom panels identify the four largest contributors at two different peaks of the lower route: protein at 1.54 nm (nanometers; 1 nm = 10⁻⁹ meters) and combined at 2.97 nm. Protein residues and later lipids both obstruct this candidate. Distances are path arc lengths, not simulation time; positive LJ (an atomic interaction potential; only its positive repulsive part is summed in our clash scans) repulsion is a clash diagnostic, not a free-energy profile.

title: A controlled test of coordinated motion
caption: Proposed next iteration: compare small guided ligand (a molecule that can bind to a receptor; here, the tested odorant) movements followed by local relaxation with a matched no-pull condition. Track the timing of side-chain, lipid and water rearrangements relative to ligand motion. This diagram describes a future comparison; it does not show an established mechanism or (odorant receptor, the odor-selective subunit) ( Zhao et al., 2024 ) a completed experiment.

title: 受體選擇背後的反應資料
caption: 整理後的全部 2,640 組 Hallem 受體–氣味反應。欄位依氣味 ID 排序，CSV 提供化學名稱；紅、藍表示正向及負向記錄反應。這些是公開電生理測量，並非團隊新做的實驗。 公開資料來源: ( Hallem & Carlson, 2006 ) .

title: 挑選第一輪受體
caption: 五個受體篩選組的公開反應平均值，比較選定的霉味相關氣味與對照。Or35a （本研究設計組合中的黑腹果蠅 Drosophila melanogaster 氣味受體名稱） 、Or22a 在此組合中呈現較大的正向差異。數據來自文獻，並非團隊新做的功能實驗；組合偏好不代表霉菌專一性。 公開資料來源: ( Hallem & Carlson, 2006 ) .

title: 預測比較
caption: 未見受體的反應預測：序列資訊提高 R² （決定係數；1 為完全吻合，0 與平均值基準相當，負值表示比此基準差） ；全部特徵相對於配體 （能與受體結合的分子，此處指受測氣味分子） ＋序列僅增加 0.0031（配對 95% 區間 −0.0316 至 0.0344）。數值來自 2,640 組受體–氣味配對的一致折外預測，並非生物介入實驗結果。 公開資料來源: ( Hallem & Carlson, 2006 ) .

caption: 未見化學群集與未見受體的控制特徵消融。L：配體 （能與受體結合的分子，此處指受測氣味分子） ；S：序列／ESM2 （蛋白語言模型；此處將胺基酸序列轉為數值特徵） ( Lin et al., 2023 ) ；P：口袋 （受體內可容納配體的局部凹穴） ；D：docking （分子對接：搜尋分子在受體中的位置與朝向，並計算分數） ( Trott & Olson, 2010 ) ／接觸；M：多姿態。各組使用相同資料、模型設定與切分。完整模型對未見受體相較 LS 的小幅增益區間包含零，不能單憑柱高判定顯著性。 公開資料來源: ( Hallem & Carlson, 2006 ) .

caption: 同一批 109 種氣味的比較。全部版本保留分子量及序列特徵；另一組固定權重用於敏感度分析，並非挑選最高分模型。化學類群留出針對下游反應標籤，上游可能已看過分子資訊。 ( Lee et al., 2023 ; Barsainyan et al., 2023 )

title: 預測反應與實測反應對照
caption: 化學類群留出的折外預測，比較原模型與加入 POM （Principal Odor Map；OpenPOM 為其開源重現版，用來學習分子氣味特徵） ( Lee et al., 2023 ; Barsainyan et al., 2023 ) 。每點為一組受體–氣味配對；共用受體與化合物，並非彼此獨立的實驗重複。虛線表示預測與實測完全一致。 ( Hallem & Carlson, 2006 )

title: 考慮不確定度後，是否仍有增益？
caption: 點為加入特徵的 ΔR² （兩個比較模型之間的 R² 差值） ，線為條件於固定預測的配對分組 bootstrap （對資料或群組重抽樣，以評估統計不確定度） 95% 區間。各列使用自己的可用子集與相配基準，並非同一資料上的特徵排行榜。區間跨零不能建立可靠增益；次要區間未校正多重比較。

title: 候選突變是否改善氣味組合偏好？
caption: 在相同 docking （分子對接：搜尋分子在受體中的位置與朝向，並計算分數） 搜尋框下，比較突變與各自的野生型受體。點為平均改變，橫線為各次搜尋的最小至最大值，不是信賴區間。偏好改變定義為「對照組平均 ΔVina （突變體 docking 分數減去相應野生型分數） − 霉味相關組平均 ΔVina」，正值有利於選定的霉味相關組；尚無候選在各次搜尋皆維持正值。此分數診斷不能證明親和力或功能改變。 結構／方法參考: ( Mirdita et al., 2022 ; Trott & Olson, 2010 ) .

title: 檢查突變機制是否合理
caption: 歷史最佳 docking （分子對接：搜尋分子在受體中的位置與朝向，並計算分數） 姿態中，突變側鏈到各氣味分子的最近距離。藍框標出 ≤4.5 Å （埃；1 Å＝0.1 奈米） 的接觸。F34Y （第 34 位：苯丙胺酸 F → 酪胺酸 Y） 、E196Q （第 196 位：麩胺酸 E → 麩醯胺酸 Q） 在這些姿態中距配體 （能與受體結合的分子，此處指受測氣味分子） 較遠；I87V （第 87 位：異白胺酸 I → 纈胺酸 V） 則說明有幾何接觸仍不代表專一性改善。數值是姿態幾何，不是結合能。 結構／方法參考: ( Mirdita et al., 2022 ; Trott & Olson, 2010 ) .

title: 果蠅模型預測與蚊子實測反應
caption: 每點為一組蚊子受體–氣味配對，涵蓋 50 個 Anopheles 受體與 40 種共同氣味，共 2,000 點。果蠅資料訓練的 ExtraTrees （以隨機切分規則建立多棵決策樹的集成模型） 基準為 R² （決定係數；1 為完全吻合，0 與平均值基準相當，負值表示比此基準差） ＝−0.288、Spearman ρ （排序相關係數，範圍 −1 至 +1；比較排序是否一致，不是百分比準確率） ＝−0.060。虛線是完全一致線，不是擬合趨勢。實測反應來自 Carey 等人，預測來自本專案；資料點共享受體及氣味，並非獨立生物重複。 公開資料來源: ( Hallem & Carlson, 2006 ; Carey et al., 2010 ) .

title: 以序列方法尋找功能相似受體
caption: 主要 48 × 24 受體配對集合上的全部十二種序列方法。點表示序列分數與 40 種氣味反應輪廓 Pearson （衡量數值輪廓線性相似程度的相關係數） 相似性的排序相關性，橫線是受體 bootstrap （對資料或群組重抽樣，以評估統計不確定度） 區間。最佳 31-aa （胺基酸殘基數） 雙向配對法 Spearman ρ （排序相關係數，範圍 −1 至 +1；比較排序是否一致，不是百分比準確率） ＝0.141，但 BH （Benjamini–Hochberg 多重檢定校正；此處 q 為校正後的 p 值） ( Benjamini & Hochberg, 1995 ) 校正 q＝0.259 未達 0.05；方法也在同一矩陣上選出。這是探索性的輪廓比對，尚非已驗證的氣味反應預測。 公開資料來源: ( Hallem & Carlson, 2006 ; Carey et al., 2010 ) .

title: 補建 Orco 區域的不確定性
caption: 8V02 （PDB 結構編號：實驗解析、已結合鄰甲酚的 OR10–Orco 複合體） 三段缺失 Orco （氣味受體共同受體，與辨識氣味的 OR 一起組成離子通道） 區域的 AlphaFold （從蛋白序列預測三維結構的 AI 系統） 信心摘要。較高 pLDDT （局部結構預測信心分數，範圍 0–100；越高表示模型越有信心） 代表較高局部信心，較大迴圈對核心 PAE （預測對齊誤差，估計殘基彼此相對位置的不確定度；越低越有信心） 代表相對位置更不確定；244–312 長迴圈的定位尤其不確定。信心值來自模板預測，不能驗證後續補建與鬆弛座標。 結構／方法參考: ( Zhao et al., 2024 ; Jumper et al., 2021 ) .

title: 原始結合態 MD 的診斷結果
caption: 已完成的 20 ns （奈秒，10⁻⁹ 秒） 結合態軌跡。曲線為 0.1 ns 區間中位數；氫鍵幾何則使用區間內符合條件的比例。底色標示預先指定的 15–20 ns 分析窗口。溫度與膜指標須連同仍持續的補建區域漂移判讀；幾何檢查通過，不能證明平衡、結合親和力或迴圈已經實驗驗證。

title: 氣味分子位於複合體的哪裡？
caption: 實驗結構 PDB （Protein Data Bank，保存分子三維結構的資料庫） ( Berman et al., 2000 ) 8V02 （PDB 結構編號：實驗解析、已結合鄰甲酚的 OR10–Orco 複合體） 的 Cα （α 碳原子，用來描述蛋白質主鏈骨架） 骨架與 o-cresol （鄰甲酚，又稱 2-methylphenol；8V02 中觀察到的氣味分子） 重原子。藍綠為 OR10 （埃及斑蚊 Aedes aegypti 的第 10 號氣味受體） ，灰綠為三個 Orco （氣味受體共同受體，與辨識氣味的 OR 一起組成離子通道） ，橘色為氣味分子。未解析區段保持斷開；米色區帶是同源轉移的膜方向參考，不是觀察到的脂質。此圖呈現結構起點，並非 MD （分子動力學：依力場逐步計算原子如何運動） ( Eastman et al., 2024 ) 軌跡。 實驗結構來源: ( Zhao et al., 2024 ) .

title: 無氣味分子的 MD 中，哪些區域在移動？
caption: 兩個 apo （未結合氣味分子的狀態） 補建起始模型的 5 ns （奈秒，10⁻⁹ 秒） 實際軌跡。三項指標皆以已解析核心的 Cα （α 碳原子，用來描述蛋白質主鏈骨架） 對齊，量測相對各自起始結構的位移。補建區域包含複合體中原先缺失的建模部分，不限於 OR10 （埃及斑蚊 Aedes aegypti 的第 10 號氣味受體） ( Zhao et al., 2024 ) 。底色的前 1 ns 包含升溫與分階段解除限制，後 4 ns 無位置限制。補建區域較大的運動提醒我們檢查結構不確定性；短程軌跡不能證明已達平衡或補建構型正確。

title: 氣味反應排序
caption: 同一公開鈣反應 assay （依特定條件進行的生物活性測試） 中 29 種氣味的回溯性排序。點為 Spearman ρ （排序相關係數，範圍 −1 至 +1；比較排序是否一致，不是百分比準確率） ，橫線為探索性的氣味重抽樣區間，未涵蓋實驗測量誤差。MD （分子動力學：依力場逐步計算原子如何運動） ( Eastman et al., 2024 ) 構型集合未優於靜態 8V00 （PDB 結構編號：實驗解析、未結合氣味分子的 OR10–Orco 複合體） ( Zhao et al., 2024 ) ；芳香環數量（ρ＝0.790）是檢視氣味組合後追加的探索性化學基準。 公開資料來源: ( Bohbot et al., 2011 ) .

title: 從每個氣味分子看相關性
caption: 每格呈現相同的 29 種氣味。將本研究 docking （分子對接：搜尋分子在受體中的位置與朝向，並計算分數） ( Trott & Olson, 2010 ) 分數與 Bohbot 等人（2011）圖 2 讀取的 AaOR10 （埃及斑蚊 Aedes aegypti 的第 10 號氣味受體） ( Zhao et al., 2024 ) 鈣反應比較；反應值是文獻測量，並非本團隊濕實驗結果。橫軸將 Vina （AutoDock Vina 對接分數；在此模型中越低越有利，並非實測反應大小） ( Eberhardt et al., 2021 ) 分數反向，預測 docking 較有利者在右側；顏色區分是否具有芳香環。相近分數仍對應不同反應，構型集合 docking 尚未建立可校準的敏感度或 EC50 （在指定功能測試中，產生一半最大反應所需的濃度） 預測。 公開資料來源: ( Bohbot et al., 2011 ) .

title: 第一套功能資料與靜態 docking 對照
caption: 上：公開 AaegOR10 （埃及斑蚊 Aedes aegypti 的第 10 號氣味受體） ( Zhao et al., 2024 ) ／AaegOrco （埃及斑蚊的氣味受體共同受體） 卵母細胞電流，以 3-methylindole 正規化；每種氣味九個卵母細胞，顯示平均 ± SEM （平均值標準誤，描述估計平均值的不確定度） 。正規化參考的 SEM 為零，不代表原始測量沒有變異。下：本研究靜態 docking （分子對接：搜尋分子在受體中的位置與朝向，並計算分數） ( Trott & Olson, 2010 ) 分數與相同七個反應平均比較。Assay （依特定條件進行的生物活性測試） 與結構複合體使用不同 Orco （氣味受體共同受體，與辨識氣味的 OR 一起組成離子通道） ，篩選濃度仍待核實；本組與 29 種氣味的鈣訊號 assay 分開分析。 公開資料來源: ( Pullmann-Lindsley et al., 2024 ) .

title: 三種增加接觸機會的設計
caption: 以起始放置方式，區分分子擴散到受體與進入口袋 （受體內可容納配體的局部凹穴） 。橘色表示氣味分子起點，第一格的水相與界面為兩種替代配置；圖中沒有畫出實際進入軌跡。已分析模擬中，增加可接觸分子或縮短起始距離仍未建立持續進入；濃度比較屬探索性研究。

title: 嘗試進入時的距離與接觸變化
caption: 外部水相、脂膜界面與入口附近放置後的實際無位置限制軌跡，以 20 ps （皮秒，10⁻¹² 秒） 區間中位數繪圖。A／B 表示兩個起始模型，納入這些配置的全部已分析軌跡。虛線分別為進入條件：距口袋 （受體內可容納配體的局部凹穴） ≤0.5 nm （奈米；1 nm＝10⁻⁹ 公尺） ，且接觸至少 4 個口袋殘基（距離 ≤0.45 nm），兩者須同時持續 100 ps。完整影格分析未見進入。三組觀察窗分別為 2 ns （奈秒，10⁻⁹ 秒） 與 10 ns，不能用本圖估計相對進入機率。

title: 施力的對象不同，問題也不同
caption: 左：SMD （牽引式分子動力學：在 MD 中加入外力引導運動） ( Isralewitz et al., 2001 ) 以彈簧將氣味分子連接到移動目標。右：另一流程引導 S3／S6 （OR10 第三與第六段跨膜螺旋的結構編號） ( Zhao et al., 2024 ) 參考距離，分子本身不受直接牽引。藍色箭頭表示施加的引導，不是觀察到的軌跡。兩種方法皆研究受控條件，不能據此量測自然進出速率。

title: 入口運動與分子移出是不同的指標
caption: 兩個起始構型的 70 ns （奈秒，10⁻⁹ 秒） 軌跡。上方為 S3／S6 （OR10 第三與第六段跨膜螺旋的結構編號） ( Zhao et al., 2024 ) 參考距離相對 apo （未結合氣味分子的狀態） 值的誤差，下方為氣味分子到口袋 （受體內可容納配體的局部凹穴） 中心的距離。為方便閱讀，以每 0.1 ns 區間的中位數繪線；底色標示最後撤除偏置的區間。完整保存影格分析未見持續移出；入口距離誤差降低不等同通道可通行。

title: 直接看 MD 保存的結構
caption: 同一條入口引導 A 軌跡在 7.6、27.6、69 與 70 ns （奈秒，10⁻⁹ 秒） 保存的座標。所有影格以 OR10 （埃及斑蚊 Aedes aegypti 的第 10 號氣味受體） ( Zhao et al., 2024 ) Cα （α 碳原子，用來描述蛋白質主鏈骨架） 對齊第一格，採相同投影與比例。藍綠與紫色標出鄰近口袋 （受體內可容納配體的局部凹穴） 的 117–139、281–299 區段，橘色是實際 o-cresol （鄰甲酚，又稱 2-methylphenol；8V02 中觀察到的氣味分子） 重原子；最後一格位於撤除偏壓之後。局部幾何改變時，配體 （能與受體結合的分子，此處指受測氣味分子） 仍在口袋附近。二維投影不能判斷空間是否可通行，選取的快照也不代表連續進出路徑。

title: 短程與延長入口引導比較
caption: 撤力前最後 100 ps （皮秒，10⁻¹² 秒） 的入口距離 RMSE （均方根誤差：相對指定參考值的整體誤差） ，與相同時間點的無新增偏壓對照比較；各起始構型分開呈現。延長流程同時改變目標漸變與固定時間。RMSE 降低表示更接近選定 apo （未結合氣味分子的狀態） 距離，不等於通道更寬或可通行；這是相關軌跡間的描述性比較。

title: 完整分子測試前的候選空隙
caption: 同一條受引導軌跡的候選球形探針半徑下界，比較 0.10、0.05 nm （奈米；1 nm＝10⁻⁹ 公尺） 網格，以及僅蛋白、蛋白加脂質障礙；空心三角形為細網格評估。各障礙模型從相同候選集中選路，但可能選到不同路徑。這是靜態中心線診斷，不是觀察到的配體 （能與受體結合的分子，此處指受測氣味分子） 軌跡，各時間點也非獨立實驗；網格敏感度限制了通道寬度已收斂的推論。

title: Inline method schematic
caption: 概念示意，並非分子軌跡或已驗證通道。綠色代表受體環境，米色圓點為附近脂質，橘色為氣味分子。候選幾何、立體可行性與實際通行，必須分開檢驗。
note: Diagram is built directly in the HTML.

title: 配體是否跟得上牽引目標？
caption: 沿兩條候選走廊、以兩種名義目標速度進行的向外 SMD （牽引式分子動力學：在 MD 中加入外力引導運動） ( Isralewitz et al., 2001 ) 。時間從共同的 0.1 ns （奈秒，10⁻⁹ 秒） 基線之後起算，曲線為 20 ps （皮秒，10⁻¹² 秒） 區間中位數。落後距離或施力過大時固定目標，因此出現平台。目標沿路進度、配體 （能與受體結合的分子，此處指受測氣味分子） 至口袋 （受體內可容納配體的局部凹穴） 距離、偏壓力是三種不同指標：目標前進並未建立分子逃離。這些模擬中受體與周圍環境可動；施加的力不是量得的自然移出能障。

title: 多等待一段時間，能否解除局部受阻？
caption: 較慢牽引條件出現落後後，將目標固定。本圖呈現總等待時間由 0.5 延長至 2 ns （奈秒，10⁻⁹ 秒） 的部分，保留原始 2 ps （皮秒，10⁻¹² 秒） 取樣。跟上條件須同時滿足沿路落後距離 ≤0.20 nm （奈米；1 nm＝10⁻⁹ 公尺） 與偏壓力 ≤100 kJ/mol/nm（約 166 pN）；橘色菱形標示同時達標的個別影格。這些短暫事件未持續 100 ps，也未觀察到持續移出。於已測時間窗內，延長局部等待仍未解除受阻。

title: 換一個受體構型，就有路可走嗎？
caption: 選定完整分子路線中，蛋白加脂質的最高 Lennard–Jones （描述原子交互作用的位能；此處碰撞掃描只加總其中的正值排斥部分） 正值排斥。各起始構型在列出時間取快照，分別評估兩條走廊。較低值表示此診斷中的嚴重碰撞較少，不代表已驗證可通行；最低的沿路峰值仍遠高於原始結合姿態參考。這些數值不是自由能障，相關快照也不是獨立實驗。

title: 定位候選路徑上的阻礙
